# The Cost of Intelligence, Episode 12: Fable 5.2 Costs 2.8x More Than Opus


### Garry Tan finds the cheapest upgrade is not upgrading, Nvidia caps its lease guarantees at $108.5 billion, Blackwell traces turn up in Chinese open models, and a petition asks for Jensen back.


[Strong Compute](https://substack.com/@strongcompute)


Nov 16, 2026


*Listen to this episode on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/66pUz46EuIHUEEtIIFYEEu) or watch it on [YouTube](https://youtu.be/KNlNnvwDYJ8) .*


Welcome back to


**The Cost of Intelligence** , our comedy news show about the money behind AI. Each episode, Ben Sand reads the industry’s invoice and asks one question: are you getting more intelligence per dollar?


This week: Garry Tan ran Claude’s two big models through Claude Code on the same 52 coding tasks. The new Fable 5.2 cost 2.8 times as much per solved task as Opus, for scores too close to call. Same grades, pricier school. Nvidia’s August filing caps its guarantees on customer leases at $108.5 billion, most of it backing one Ohio campus leased to OpenAI. Nvidia used to sell the shovels. Now it’s the mine’s emergency contact. A former OpenAI researcher says six Chinese open models carry traces of Nvidia’s Blackwell chips, which are banned for export to China. And Elon Musk and other tech executives signed a petition asking Nvidia’s board to bring Jensen Huang back. Here’s the written version, with every source linked.


---


## The tokens


AI reads and writes in tokens, chunks of words.


The world runs about


**469 trillion tokens a day** , on


[tokensperday.com](https://tokensperday.com/) ’s live model as of 15 November (a July estimate, grown to today). That’s up about


**2 trillion** since Friday’s show. The tokens worked the weekend. Overtime’s on you.


On the site’s own path, that’s about


**518 trillion a day by New Year’s Eve** . The tokens already have New Year’s plans. Your budget wasn’t invited.


---


## The landlord’s rate card


*“A small weekend discount, darling. Don’t get used to it.”*


On the Ornn Compute Price Index, which tracks actual rentals, as of the 14 November settle:


-


**NVIDIA H100** settled at


**$3.19 an hour** , down about


**6%** since Friday’s show and about


**2%** over the month (


[Ornn H100](https://data.ornn.com/api/public-index/gpu/H100%20SXM/index-history) ). The landlord gave back Friday’s raise. He kept the deposit.


-


**B200** settled at


**$9.66 an hour** , down about


**1%** since Friday, but up about


**22%** over the month (


[Ornn B200](https://data.ornn.com/api/public-index/gpu/B200/index-history) ). The landlord left a mint on the pillow.


---


## Chips, power and the work


**Chips.** Epoch counts about


**34 million AI chips** , measured in Nvidia H100s, its latest count, from 21 October (


[Epoch AI](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-chip-sales) ).


**Power.** AI data centres draw about


**30 gigawatts** . That’s our estimate, built on


[Epoch AI’s data-centre tracker](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-data-centers) . The International Energy Agency’s figure for last year puts AI at about


**half a percent of the world’s electricity** , which is about


**a tenth of a percent** of all the energy we use, our estimate (


[Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/how-much-energy-do-data-centers-and-artificial-intelligence-use) ). Too small to notice. Big enough to need its own substation.


**The work.** Our name for it this week is


**SI: Seller-backed Intelligence** . Intelligence where the store that sold you the couch also guarantees your apartment.


On our bet, SI does about


**11.7% of the hours we work** , about


**41 minutes a day** for everyone on a payroll. Our number ticked up a hair with the token count. Workers themselves say it saves them about


**2% of their hours** , per the St. Louis Fed’s July survey (


[FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/RPSGENAITSALL) ). That’s about seven minutes a day. SI just learned what middle management feels like.


These numbers are a work in progress. Got better data? Step boldly into our DMs.


---


## The news: Nvidia’s filing


Nvidia’s August quarterly filing caps its guarantees on customer leases at


**$108.5 billion** (


[Nvidia 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000075/nvda-20260726.htm) ). That’s more than all of Nvidia’s sales in that same quarter, about $96.2 billion (


[Nvidia CFO commentary](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000073/q2fy27cfocommentary.htm) ).


Nvidia only pays if a customer stops paying its lease.


-


Most of it,


**$105 billion** , backs one campus in Ohio, leased to OpenAI.


-


The other


**$3.5 billion** covers other AI clouds.


Nvidia sells you the chips, then vouches for your rent. Every parent of a college kid knows that deal.


The Ohio campus is planned at about


**4.25 gigawatts** . It goes up in nine phases, and the first isn’t due before 2028. Nine phases. Even the data centre is on a payment plan.


*Per-dollar verdict: the cheapest chip is the one somebody else is on the hook for.*


---


## Chips in China


Will DePue used to be a researcher at OpenAI. He says he found traces of Nvidia’s Blackwell chips inside


**six Chinese open models** : the way their weights were set up matches Blackwell, not the older Hopper chips (


[The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/former-openai-researcher-says-he-found-nvidia-blackwell-fingerprints-hidden-inside-six-chinese-ai-models/) ;


[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/13/export-banned-nvidia-chips-are-behind-chinas-most-powerful-ai-models-uh-oh-jensen/) ;


[The Register](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/11/13/chinese-ai-labs-are-training-models-on-nvidias-blackwell-despite-export-controls-says-ex-openai-engineer/5309891) ).


[will depue @willdepue I have a major result to share. I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China. This sounds insane, … 9:29 PM · Nov 12, 2026 · 6.59M Views 1.81K Replies · 6.37K Reposts · 41K Likes](https://x.com/willdepue/status/2120992457630326841)


The list includes DeepSeek’s V4 models and Kimi K3. He says it shows they had access to the chips. He can’t say how they got them, or where the training ran. They may be free weights, but they’ve been training at an Equinox gym.


They’re not just fit, they’re popular too. This week, Chinese models carried


**more than eight in ten tokens** on OpenRouter’s top ten list (


[OpenRouter rankings](https://openrouter.ai/rankings) ).


*Per-dollar verdict: the cheapest tokens may depend on the priciest chips.*


---


## Nvidia’s boardroom


Nvidia announced Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday, and now there’s a push to bring him back.


Elon Musk and other tech executives signed a petition asking the board to reinstate him (


[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/14/elon-musk-other-tech-execs-sign-petition-calling-on-nvidia-to-reinstate-jensen-huang/) ). The petition says it has


**more than 100,000 signatures** . Ben can’t get four people to sign a birthday card.


[Elon Musk @elonmusk @yunta_tsai A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too 8:51 PM · Nov 13, 2026 · 10.6M Views 7.47K Replies · 20.2K Reposts · 228K Likes](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2121345211959804234)


Investors


**Brad Gerstner** of Altimeter and


**Gavin Baker** of Atreides wrote to the board too, asking it to keep the door open to his return (


[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/14/nvidia-investors-jensen-huang-return-board-letter.html) ).


[Brad Gerstner @altcap This letter was sent to the Nvidia Board today which we believe outlines the minimum acceptable standards the Board owes shareholders as it manages this difficult situation. Onward. 🫡 11:47 PM · Nov 13, 2026 · 1.62M Views 1.16K Replies · 1.83K Reposts · 18.1K Likes](https://x.com/altcap/status/2121389561414623679)


Nvidia reports earnings on


**Tuesday, 17 November** . The board has a petition, an investor letter and an earnings date. Its inbox needs an inbox.


*Per-dollar verdict: 100,000 signatures, zero discounts.*


---


## The tier list


How many dollars of API usage you get per dollar of subscription, on our 15 November run of Adam Holter’s method with


[Real API Pricing](https://github.com/Fei2411/real-api-pricing) . And they’re off!


[Adam Holter @AdamHoltererer Subsidization varies across users and usage patterns Some users get a lot more subsidization than others, but all of them get a ton This could be because the API rates for different types of tokens, such as cached input and output, might be different than the usage rates 10:51 PM · Nov 7, 2026 · 11.9K Views 8 Replies · 2 Reposts · 104 Likes](https://x.com/AdamHoltererer/status/2119201175904149984)


-


**Claude Max** breaks first, at about


**$77** of API value per plan dollar.


-


**Claude Ultra** runs second at about


**$66** , and


**Claude Pro** is a neck behind in third at about


**$64** . Claude takes win, place and show. Somebody check who owns the track.


-


Then a gap, and into the turn comes the pack: Claude Max on Haiku about


**$55** , Google AI Ultra on Flash about


**$49** , Claude Ultra on Haiku about


**$47** , Claude Pro on Haiku about


**$46** , and X Ultra at about


**$44** , its floor.


-


Ninth and tenth:


**ChatGPT’s two Pro plans** , about


**$28** and


**$27** .


-


Trailing the field, last of 44:


**Google AI Pro on Gemini Argon** , at about


**$1.40** . Argon hasn’t even left the paddock.


On 1 December, Argon’s API price doubles (


[Gemini API pricing](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing) ). Same model, double the bill. That’s not an upgrade. That’s a cover charge.


This whole board has held steady since Friday. Nobody’s passing anybody. The finish is a photocopy.


---


## Department of Token Efficiency


Three cuts today. We’ve sharpened the chain.


**Cut one: Garry Tan, the head of Y Combinator.** He ran two of Claude’s big models through Claude Code on the same


**52 coding tasks** (


[Garry Tan on X](https://x.com/garrytan/status/2121464508225053153) ;


[g-harness-evals](https://github.com/garrytan/g-harness-evals) ).


[Garry Tan @garrytan Keep Opus 5.5 as your coding default in Claude Code. On 52 coding tasks in Claude Code 2.1.322, Fable 5.2 solved about as many (82.7% vs 84.6%) but cost 2.80x as much per solved task. Opus already solves most of these tasks, though, so telling the two apart will take harder … 4:45 AM · Nov 14, 2026 · 139K Views 233 Replies · 48 Reposts · 727 Likes](https://x.com/garrytan/status/2121464508225053153)


-


The new model,


**Fable 5.2** , solved


**83%** of the tasks.


**Opus** did a bit better at


**85%** . Too close to call.


-


But per solved task, Fable cost


**$1.83** and Opus only


**$0.65** . That’s


**2.8 times** as much.


-


Tan’s advice: keep Opus as your coding default. Same grades, pricier school.


One poster on X said Fable ate their whole weekly limit in 20 minutes (


[PrecyartG on X](https://x.com/PrecyartG/status/2121590456643457246) ). Brunch lasts longer.


Then Tan kept the model and swapped the harness. On Opus,


**OpenClaw** cost


**40 cents** per solved task and


**Claude Code 21 cents** . Nearly double, on the same model. Tan won’t crown a best harness. Swap the harness, keep the brain: half the bill goes down the drain.


**The fine print:** Tan’s own test. 52 tasks for the models, 20 for the harness. Y Combinator has a stake in two of the harnesses, and two add-ons he tested are his own. Side effects may include sudden loyalty to the model you already have.


**Cut two: Deepnote** , which makes data notebooks. It priced a month of an AI agent watching one company’s Slack (


[Deepnote](https://deepnote.com/research/benchmark) ).


-


On Fable, it came to about


**$4,700** a month.


-


**OpenAI’s Sol** did it for


**$281** . That’s


**94% less** , and Sol finished second on Deepnote’s scoreboard.


-


Agents that butt in cost


**1.8 times** as much as agents that wait their turn. Finally, a benchmark for the guy who talks in every stand-up.


**The fine print:** Deepnote’s own benchmark, 50 workplace scenarios. The monthly bill is Deepnote’s extrapolation, not an invoice. Ask your manager if reply-all is right for you.


**Cut three: HeyGen** , which makes AI video. It built its own harness for video work, called


**HyperFrames** , and ran


**17 video tasks** on the same model (


[HeyGen](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/blog/how-we-build-our-coding-harness-for-video) ).


-


HyperFrames cost


**30% less** than Claude Code.


-


It needed


**35% fewer** model turns.


-


A judge model rated the results even.


Even Claude Code pays a generalist tax. The specialist gets a refund.


**The fine print:** a vendor grading its own product. Percentages only, no dollar figure. 17 tasks, judged by a model, not by people. Results not typical. Your video may vary.


Still: chainsaw approved.
